final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with locked labor enforcement (immediate suspension, Jan 1 2020 effective date), 3.6-3.9% dairy access, and 75% RVC with an 18-month transition for existing auto lines. However, the sunset clause remained unresolved—USTR demanded month-55 objection/day-1826 termination while Canada sought a mandatory renegotiation window, creating ratification uncertainty.
minority_objections: Canada insisted on mandatory renegotiation window before sunset termination, which USTR rejected as a Congressional deal-killer
Labor union raised concerns that 18-month existing-line transition could create enforcement loopholes if wage audits were also delayed
key_conflicts: Sunset mechanism: USTR's hard termination (month-55 objection, day-1826 end) vs Canada's mandatory renegotiation window
Auto RVC phase-in: USTR demanded day-one 75% vs Mexico/Canada sought 18-month transition for existing lines
Labor enforcement retroactivity: whether wage violations during restructuring period would trigger immediate suspension
key_concessions: Canada moved from initial resistance to 3.9% dairy access in exchange for locked labor enforcement language
USTR accepted 18-month transition for existing auto lines (from initial day-one 75% demand)
Mexico accepted immediate suspension labor enforcement with no cure window (from initial 60-day proposal)
Canada accepted forward-looking enforcement only (no retroactive violations during restructuring)
red_lines: USTR: no mandatory renegotiation window in sunset clause (Congressional certainty requirement)
Canada: real-time labor monitors with immediate suspension power must be in drafted text before dairy concession
Labor union: wage enforcement must apply to all production from Jan 1 2020, not just new models
Congress: labor violations must trigger tariffs, not advisory recommendations
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Supply chain dual-track sourcing costs during 18-month transition were raised but never resolved in text
Dairy access term uncertainty (whether it survives agreement lapse) was flagged but not answered
Chapter 19 dispute settlement—Canada's stated redline in opening—disappeared from discussion after Round 1
downstream_risk_variables: Sunset clause language remains unresolved—creates ongoing ratification uncertainty in all three countries
Auto industry phase-in mechanics (ramp vs restructure deadline) not finalized despite repeated requests
Dairy access term language not locked—creates investment uncertainty for U.S. producers
Dual-track sourcing compliance costs during transition could surface as implementation crisis
uncertainty_notes: Sunset mechanism unresolved (USTR vs Canada positions 4+ points apart on package_progress impact). Auto phase-in mechanics requested by industry 4+ times but never answered in text. Dairy term language flagged but not locked. Chapter 19 vanished after R1 despite being Canada's stated redline.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC day-one vs 18-month transition drove 4 rounds of negotiation; USTR's concession to Mexico's split proposal was decisive in advancing package_progress +5 in R3
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress stated 'won't touch this unless violations have teeth'; USTR's immediate-suspension language (no cure window) was the concrete proposal that unlocked Canada's dairy concession and drove us_ratification_risk -5 in R3
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada explicitly tied 3.9% dairy access to seeing labor enforcement 'drafted and in the doc this round'; dairy concession was the stated price for Canada joining the package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada mentioned Chapter 19 in opening statement but it never resurfaced—no proposals, no follow-up, no impact on outcomes
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Sunset drove every round after R2; Mexico's 5-year review with 180-day notice was the compromise proposal that reduced sunset_uncertainty -5 and advanced package; USTR's rejection of Canada's renegotiation window was the stated reason for ongoing impasse
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'won't pass the Senate' if Canada walks; USTR justified hard sunset and immediate labor enforcement as Congressional requirements; ratification constraints shaped multiple concrete proposals (labor panel, sunset terms)
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply chain manufacturers raised dual-track sourcing costs and phase-in mechanics 3 times but received no resolution; flagged as concern but did not alter any proposal or concession
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Canada referenced needing to 'join the package' after U.S.-Mexico locked 75% RVC, but this was background context; no participant cited it as the reason for a specific concession or proposal

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
